name: Research Project Semiannual Progress Report
intro_text: Please upload a Word document of no more than 2 pages covering your accomplishments, your plans for the next period, and any changes. Suggested file name convention example: Cain_Accomplishments.

about: Your semiannual progress report summarizes your accomplishments, plans, and changes.
It feeds directly into the Center’s Research Performance Progress Report (RPPR) to NIH.

sections.title: Accomplishments
sections.instructions:
Your document should contain the following:
- Activities
- Objectives
- Significant Results
- Key Outcomes
- Unmet Goals

For Projects:
- What experiments you completed (give reference to aims/milestones/timeline)
- What you found
- Dissemination of Information

For Cores:
- Implementations of renovations, building of core
- Core activity and use

sections.title: Plans
sections.instructions:
Please provide a summary of what you plan to do during the next reporting period to accomplish your project goals and objectives. Please discuss efforts to ensure that the approach continues to be scientifically rigorous and results are robust and unbiased.
Please remember that significant changes in objectives and scope require prior approval of the agency (e.g., NIH Grants Policy Statement, 8.1.2.). Please include any important modifications to the original plans. Please provide a scientific justification for any changes involving research with human subjects or vertebrate animals. A detailed description of such changes must be provided under Changes.

sections.title: Changes
sections.instructions: Please describe challenges or delays encountered during the reporting period and actions or plans to resolve those challenges. Please describe only significant challenges that may impede the research (e.g., accrual of patients, hiring of personnel, need for resources or research tools) and emphasize their resolution.

sections.title: Evidence of Esteem
sections.instructions: Please give evidence of esteem in your uploaded document. Examples are invited talks and service on review panels or editorial boards.

sections.title: Quick Research Performance Progress Report (RPPR) questions
sections.instructions: NIH asks these questions in the RPPR for each project and core every year. Most answers are No.

questions.prompt: B.1.a Have the major goals changed since the initial competing award or previous report?

questions.help_text: If you answered Yes, please explain here.

questions.prompt: C.3 Did this work produce new technologies or techniques during this reporting period?

questions.help_text: If you answered Yes, please explain here.

questions.prompt: C.4 Did it produce inventions, patent applications, or licenses during this reporting period?

questions.help_text: If you answered Yes, please explain here.

questions.prompt: C.5.a Did it produce other significant products, such as databases, software, models, or instruments?

questions.help_text: If you answered Yes, please explain here.

questions.prompt: C.5.c Is data from this work being shared as its Data Management and Sharing plan describes?

questions.help_text: If you answered No, please explain here.

questions.prompt: F.3 Were there significant changes to human subjects, vertebrate animals, biohazards, or select agents?

questions.help_text: If you answered Yes, please explain here.

questions.prompt: G.9 Was any significant part of this work done outside the United States, or by someone employed by a foreign organization?

questions.help_text: If you answered Yes, please explain here.

sections.title: Research team (RPPR section D.1)
sections.instructions:
Please list everyone who worked on this project or core during this budget year, including you. Please use one row per person.
Please give effort in person months.
- Calendar months = 12-month appointments
- Academic months = 9-month appointments
- Summer months = 3-month appointments

questions.prompt: eRA Commons ID (if they have one)
Role on this project or core
